label: paragraph_title
text: DRUNKEN BRAWL.

label: text
text: R.G.A. MEN GET INTO TROUBLE.

label: text
text: ASSAULT ON POLICE.

label: text
text: Before Mr. R. E. Lindsell at the Central Magistracy this morning, Driver A. E. Blackman, of 38th Heavy Battery, and Gunner Kamm, of Victoria Barracks, were charged on four counts of damaging public ricshas, drunk and disorderly behaviour, and breaking the. cells of the charge room. Kamm was charged in addition with assaulting an Indian constable in the charge room.

label: text
text: The evidence disclosed that after 11 p.m. on Friday the defendants while in a drunken state damaged two ricshas left at the junction of Peel Street and Queen's Road Central. They were arrested by two Indian constables and brought to the charge room where the second defendant pinched one of the constables with his clenched fist.

label: text
text: Sub-Inspector C. McNab Wilson stated in evidence that he was in the charge room when the defendants were brought in at 12.30 a.m. They were both badly under the influence of liquor, and the second defendant was very violent in his behaviour, refusing to submit to a search or answer questions, and later knocking down an Indian constable in his presence. The first defendant walked quietly to the cell, but four European officers had to assist in placing the second defendant in the cell. The prisoners then proceeded to smash up the cells and tore off the flooring boards, keeping up a disturbance until 3:30 a.m. A military escort arrived later and took them away.

label: text
text: Both defendants accepted the evidence; Kamm stating that he did not remember any of the incidents of that night.

label: text
text: His Worship fined the first defendant $5 on each of the four charges, and a total of $5 compensation for damage to a ricsha and the cell.

label: text
text: Addressing the second defendant, His Worship said that he had aggravated his offence by striking down a constable in front of the Inspector, and he was not prepared to overlook this offence. He imposed a fine of $5 for damage to the ricsha and $4 compensation. On the charge of being drunk he was fried $5, and for damaging the cell he was ordered to pay $10 compensation. On the charge of assaulting the constable, defendant was sentenced to 14 days' hard labour.

label: paragraph_title
text: SWATOW FALLS.

label: text
text: RED ARMY ENTERING THE PORT.

label: text
text: "ANTIS" TOO PROUD TO FIGHT?

label: text
text: According to the fast wireless report to the Naval authorities the Reds are already entering the port of Swatow.

label: text
text: Since yesterday's report it has been ascertained that the Red victory was due more to internal discord in the anti-Red camp than to a grand finale.

label: text
text: At present the bulk of the anti-Red army is retreating towards the Fukien and Kiangsi borders (to the North). It also seems that the bulk of the Canton Reds are still in the field, the presumption being that only a comparatively small detachment has been sent to occupy Swatow.

label: text
text: One anti-Red detachment is surrounded as a result of the sudden debacle. It was fighting in the thick between the anti-Red centre and left, and Reds have now poured to their rear. Another force sent to extricate them stayed to deal with a rising of Farmers' Volunteers—friendly to the Reds—and was itself hemmed in before reaching the objective.

label: text
text: A feint by the Reds—the withdrawal of the Whampoa Cadets from the centre and their replacement by Cantonese—led to that last victory for Chan Kwing-ming but when the Cadets counter-attacked, the rout began.

label: text
text: The panic seems to have started in the rear rather than in the front.

label: text
text: Hopoh, the key to Kityeung, was vacated and then the Red right wing moved up in no great hurry, consolidating their gains.

label: text
text:
Russian gunners are said once more to have been the deciding factor in the struggle. Knowing that the anti-Reds were running short of ammunition and that the absence of a central authority had led to the alignment not being preserved, the Reds brought their artillery up in the salient they had made. This assault ended the resistance by the anti-Reds who were fighting and they fell back in precipitate retreat.
Up till Saturday Swatow, had been "quiet". Once 'disquieting' news came through from the front, the officials, in charge began to leave. There has been no exodus of any size to Hongkong. A Japanese steamer arrived here yesterday from Swatow and the s.s. "Sunning" also came in from Shanghai via Swatow.

label: text
text: One or two Northern Chinese warships are stated to have been at or near Swatow. The anti-Reds, before leaving, are said to have requested the Navy, to blockade Swatow so as to cut off its communication, by sea, with Canton.

label: text
text: Southern Front.

label: text
text: Disquieting news continues to arrive from the “southern front.” There is more than a possibility that the anti-Reds have lost the grip on Shekki, the capital of Heungshan district.

label: text
text: In the Sze Yap, the Reds are regaining control at the more exposed positions but the up-country is still full of anti-Red semi-irregulars.

label: text
text: Merchants Volunteers are patroing to keep order and to protect their own interests, if possible.

label: paragraph_title
text: A DEBTOR FIRM:

label: text
text:
SIEMSSEN & CO'S CLAIM
Having obtained an execution warrant in respect of money owing by a Chinese firm for goods sold, Siemssen & Co. found that a distress warrant for rent had been issued against the firm in question by the alleged landlord who claimed prior call on the money paid into Court as a result of the selling up of the debtor firm.
Siemssen & Co., through Mr. Wadeson at the court this morning, claimed that the alleged landlord was a partner in the debtor firm and that therefore his claim could not hold.
The issue before the court was

label: text
text: whether the man in question was a partner or not, and therefore whether or not he was entitled to claim before Siemsen & Co.

label: text
text: THE BARGAIN WITH SENG.

label: text
text:
Reports indicate that the Feng-
tian forces are occupying Pengpu,
and Sun Chuanfang is making his
defence line at Min-yang.

label: text
text: A detachment of Hujeh troops is reported to have left to day for Honan.

label: text
text: A telegram to Wu Pei-fu from Sun Chuan-fang states that the latter informed Feng Yu-hsiang of the advance of the allied troops to Hsuchow and called on Feng Yu-hsiang to carry out his part of the bargain "in accordance with previous understanding". It is understood that Wu Pei-fu issued a manifesto to the effect that funds of the Salt Gabelle will not be allowed to go to Peking.

label: text
text: This action is similar to the step taken by Chang Tso-lin at Mukden, and he argues that if Chang Tso-lin was allowed to do so by the foreign Flowers he can follow suit.

text: KHYENR PASS RAILWAY OPENED:

label: text
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text: Fumrud, Nov. 2

label: text
text: In the presence of a representative gathering from all over India, Sir Charles Innes, on behalf of the Viceroy, opened the new railway through the Kliyber Pass which Sir Charles in a speech, described us historical.

label: text
text:
was one of the famous highways of the world. Sir Charles said that the railway was another enduring moment in India to the genus of British engineering. It opened the Pass as it was never opened before. The result would be that trade would be developed and another link in the chain of friendship and peace had been forged. He hoped India and Afghanistan would be drawn closer in bonds of mutual advantage and neighbourly friendship.
AERIAL JAUNT

label: paragraph_title
text: WHISKY A CURE?

label: text
text: GARRISON SERGT. MAJOR'S EXPERIMENT

label: text
text: COURT MARTIAL SEQUEL.

label: text
text: Having heard, he stated in evidence this morning, that whisky was a cure for a minor ailment from which he was suffering, Garrison, Sergt. Major Henry Tye dosed himself for several days taking at no time more than four a day and mixing the alcohol with milk.

label: text
text: He was charged before a district court martial this morning with being guilty of conduct prejudicial to good order and military discipline in that he became unfit by reason of previous indulgence in alcohol stimulants.

label: text
text: He was not a spirit drinker, he said in his evidence this morning. His usual drink was beer, and the whisky evidently did not agree with him. He had, added to this, a close family bereavement which had preyed on his mind somewhat. He thought all this had combined to make the effects of the whisky more potent.

label: text
text: He was examined medically on the morning of October 19 and having been pronounced to be suffering from alcoholic poisoning was kept at the military hospital until October 24. For two days he was kept in bed, his condition having shown no signs of improvement. He was continually calling for drinks and the keys, said Capt. R. F. Walker, M.C., R.A.M.C.

label: text
text: Both Capt. Walker and Major A. S. Littlejohns, R.A.M.C. were questioned by Major Paton, who represented the prisoner, as to whether a long or short bout of drinking was likely to have brought about the state of priscner. He had only been in the hospital a short time and did not this go to show that he had not induced to any great extent asked Major Paton.

label: text
text: Both witnesses replied in effect that it depended on how much the man was accustomed to take in the ordinary way.

label: text
text: Evidence as to character was given and the prisoner's 23 years and 10 months' service, with only one minor offence against him was mentioned. Major J. Macready, D.S.O., Bfd. and Herts. Regt. also spoke as to prisoner's exemplary character since he joined the China Command in March of last year.

label: text
text:
The Court assembled later for the purpose of trying Corporal Churn on charges of absenting himself without leave and failing to report when detailed for guard.
His defence was that he had a pass to go and see the boxing and failed to hand in the half of it on his return. As regarded the absence from duty he had verbal leave from the orderly corporal.
It transpired that when this latter was given the orderly corporal did not know that the prisoner was under open arrest in connection with the first charge.

label: text
text:
Shortly after, noon yesterday, a motor cycle driven by Sanitary, Inc. species P. Knight, along Queen's Road, Bust knocked down a six-year old Chinese girl near Wing Fung Street, causing injuries to the head and legs.
The injured girl was taken to the Government Civil Hospital, but her parents turned up later and took her away contrary to the medical officer's advice.

label: paragraph_title
text: ALLEGED FRAUDS

label: text
text:
Further evidence was taken before Mr. S. H. E. McElderry at the Central Magistracy this morning in the case in which Mr. J. E. Atherley, ex-manager of Getz Bros. & Co. (of the Orient), Ltd. stands charged with alleged misappropriation of funds.
Certain points in the evidence given by the Chinese relationship of the firm were gone over when this witness was retailed and cross-examined by Mr. D. H. Blake for the prosecution.

label: text
text: Answering questions, witness stated that on April 1, 1924, he handed the manager a sum of $5,981.93 and later certain other sums which he received from dealers. On each occasion witness was given a fresh receipt by the manager in which the amount in the former receipt was included and the old ones destroyed. The last receipt was that for $13,149.84 produced in court.

label: text
text: Continuing, witness said that he prepared deposit slips shewing the amounts available for paying into the Bank. These slips were shown to the manager, who cut out some of the items by drawing a line across them. These items would appear in the receipts given by the manager. Witness further explained the difference in the sums paid into the Bank and those received from dealers by stating that some of the cheques received were used to settle items appearing in the deposit slips other than those concerning the drawers of the cheques.

label: text
text: At the Kowloon Magistracy this morning, Mr. Oscar Eager was charged with not keeping to the proper side of the road when driving his car at the junction of Nathan Road and Gascoigne Road.

label: text
text:
Magistrate (Mr. E. W. Hamilton) that the lamp post at this junction was in an awkward position and it was difficult to get round it.
In another traffic summons, Mr. D. S. Green had to answer a charge of allowing his private car to be used for public hire.
It was stated in defence that the car was parked at the Duro Garage in Nathan Road, but that one of the employees took the car out thinking that it belonged to the garage.
The case was adjourned for one week.
For disobeying a traffic signal at the junction of Nathan Road and Gascoigne Road, Mr. J. Barnet, driving a motor cycle, was fined $10.

INQUIRY INTO MISS
MACKAY'S-DEATH

label: text
text:
INQUIRY INTO MISS MACKAY'S DEATH.
The motor mishap at Laichtkok on October 28 which resulted in fatal injuries to Bessie, the thirteen-year-old daughter of Mrs Mackay, of Jordan House, Kowloon, will be the subject of a Coroner's inquiry, when the circumstances attending the fatality will be investigated.
The inquiry will be conducted by Mr. E. W. Hamilton at the Kowloon Magistracy on Thursday November 12 at 3 p.m.
